Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

stimulate verb

also stimulation, stimulating, stimulus, spur, give a boost to, stimulate the appetite, stimulate growth

classical

Liv. 1.22.2: avīta glōria animum stimulābat (Lewis & Short)

stimulō, stimulāre, stimulāvī, stimulātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

spur on, stimulate

From stimulus, a goad: to spur someone on to act. It also means to torment, to give no peace (Cic. Rosc. Am. 6); context decides. The noun stimulus is a stimulus in the same two senses.

Other words

  • acuō, acuere, acuī, acūtum — sharpen, stimulate (the mind); spur on

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 5.3.49: illōs sat aetās acuet (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 2.7 (Lewis & Short)

    Literally to sharpen a blade; then to sharpen the wits (mentem, ingenium) and to rouse a person.

  • incitō, incitāre, incitāvī, incitātum — spur on, quicken; make grow faster

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Col. 4.22.3: ut incitārī vītis possit (Lewis & Short)

    To set going fast, to urge on; of plants and rivers, to make grow or swell. The noun incitāmentum is an incentive (Cic. Arch. 23; Tac.).

Examples

  • avīta glōria animum stimulābat

    the glory of his grandfather spurred him onLiv. 1.22.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • illōs sat aetās acuet

    age will sharpen them enoughTer. Ad. 5.3.49 (Lewis & Short)

See also excite, encourage, motivation.
